title: Help Wanted: One Friendly Digger
text:
Help wanted! The Maple Street building site is looking for a friendly digger to join our team. We are building a new playground, and we need someone who can dig {adverb} and work well with others.

The right digger must have a strong scoop, bright yellow paint, and at least {number} {plural noun}. You should be able to lift heavy dirt, move big rocks, and {verb} without making a mess. Diggers who can also tell jokes about {plural noun} will get extra points.

This job is Monday to Friday. Lunch is at noon, and every digger gets a full tank of fuel and a {adjective} car wash on Fridays. You will share a parking spot with a dump truck named Gus. Gus is very nice but likes {verb ending in ing} in the morning, so please be patient.

To apply, please roll over to the trailer and ask for Foreman Pat. Bring a letter that tells us why you are the most {adjective} digger in town. We also like diggers who bring a {noun} for the break room.

title: Good Morning from Foreman Rosa
text:
Good morning, team! This is Foreman Rosa speaking on the big loudspeaker. Please put down your coffee and listen up.

Today we are pouring the floor for the new fire station. The cement truck will arrive at nine o'clock with {number} loads of cement and one load of {plural noun}. Please stay {adverb} out of the way while it backs up. It beeps very loudly, like a {adjective} {animal}.

A few reminders. Hard hats must be worn at all times, even during lunch. Please do not {verb} on the fresh cement, and please stop writing {plural noun} in it with sticks. Yesterday someone left a {noun} in the tool shed, and it is still there.

One more thing. Today is Big Mike's birthday! At lunch we will all gather by the crane and sing to him. He has asked us to sing it while {verb ending in ing}. Thank you, team, and have a {adjective} day.

title: Plans for Our Brand New Library
text:
These are the official building plans for the new Oak Hill Library. The town has saved money for {number} years to build it, so we want it to be perfect.

The library will have two floors. The front door will be painted bright {color} and will be big enough for a {animal} to walk through. In the lobby, there will be a fountain that sprays {plural noun} every hour on the hour.

The kids' room will be on the first floor. It will have bean bags, a reading tent, and a slide shaped like a giant {noun}. Children will be allowed to {verb} quietly during story time. The second floor will be for grown-ups who like to read {adverb}.

The last part of the plan is the roof. The builders will plant a garden up there full of {adjective} flowers and {plural noun}. When the library opens, the mayor will cut the ribbon and give a long talk about {verb ending in ing}.

title: Visitor Rules at the Building Site
text:
Welcome to the Pine Street building site! We are building a new pet store, and we are happy you came to watch. Please read these rules before you visit.

All visitors must stay behind the orange fence. You may wave at the workers, but please do not ask them to {verb} while they are busy. Every visitor gets a hard hat and a {adjective} vest to wear. Please give them back when you leave, even if they look good on you.

You may take pictures of the bulldozer, the crane, and the big pile of {plural noun}. Our bulldozer is named Daisy, and she gets shy if you stare at her {adverb}. The crane driver, Mr. Lopez, likes to wave back with his {body part}.

If you are hungry, the snack table has juice boxes, {food}, and a {noun} for sharing. If you have a question, ask Foreman Jill. She knows everything about bricks, cement, and {plural noun}. Thank you for visiting, and come back next week to see us {verb ending in ing} the roof.

title: The Lunch Truck Menu
text:
Every day at noon, the lunch truck parks right next to the cement mixer. Here is today's menu for hungry builders.

The Bulldozer Burger is a big burger with lettuce, tomato, and a slice of {food} on top. It comes with a side of crunchy {plural noun}. The Crane Sandwich is so tall that you have to stand on a {noun} to take a bite. The Hard Hat Soup is served in a clean hard hat and tastes very {adjective}.

For dessert, try our famous Brick Cake. It is chocolate on the outside and {color} on the inside. Workers say it makes them want to {verb} all afternoon.

Please wait in line {adverb}, and please do not feed your sandwich to the {animal} who lives behind the fence. Today's special is a smoothie made with bananas, milk, and {plural noun}. Our cook, Miss Bea, says it will make your muscles feel {adjective}.

title: Diary of a Dump Truck Named Dot
text:
Dear Diary, my name is Dot, and I am a dump truck. I am big, I am yellow, and I am very {adjective}. Today was a busy day at the building site.

In the morning, the digger filled my back with dirt. Then it filled me with rocks. Then, for some reason, it filled me with {number} {plural noun}. I drove them {adverb} to the other side of the site and dumped them in a neat pile.

At lunch, the workers sat in my shade and ate their sandwiches. A worker named Hank told a joke about a {noun}, and everyone {past tense verb}. I laughed too, but trucks laugh by honking, so I went {sound}.

This afternoon, it rained a little, and I got muddy. Tomorrow is my bath day. The workers will scrub me with soap and {plural noun} until I shine. Then I will {verb} all the way home to my garage and dream about {verb ending in ing}.

title: Week Three at the New School Building
text:
Hello, families! Here is our weekly update from the team building the new Willow Elementary School. This week we finished the walls for the gym. The gym will be big enough to hold {number} {plural noun} at the same time. We also put in the big windows, and the workers cleaned them {adverb} until they sparkled.

On Wednesday, a {adjective} surprise arrived on a truck. It was the new playground slide! It is shaped like a {noun} and is very tall. Our crane, Big Bertha, lifted it into place while everybody clapped.

Next week, the painters will paint the hallways. The principal picked the color herself. It is called Sunny {silly word}. We will also start building the lunchroom, where students will someday eat {food} and {verb} with their friends.

Thank you for being so patient while we keep {verb ending in ing}.

title: What Is Inside the Big Red Toolbox
text:
Uncle Ray is a builder, and he has a big red toolbox. Today he let me look inside and write down everything I found.

The top drawer has a hammer, a tape measure, and a pencil that is only {number} inches long. It also has a little bag of {plural noun}. Uncle Ray says he uses them for fixing {adjective} doors.

The middle drawer has screwdrivers in every size. The biggest one is as long as a {noun}. Next to the screwdrivers is a level with a bubble inside. When the bubble is in the middle, the shelf is straight. When the bubble starts {verb ending in ing}, you should try again.

The bottom drawer is the messiest one. It has gloves, safety goggles, and a very old granola bar. Uncle Ray says a good builder always works {adverb} and never forgets to {verb}. When I asked about the {plural noun} hidden in the corner, he just {past tense verb} and closed the drawer.

title: The View from the Crane Cab
text:
Dear Ellie, I am writing this letter from inside my crane. My little cab is way up high, and it has a comfy seat, a heater, and a picture of you taped to the window.

From up here, I can see the whole town. The cars look like tiny {plural noun}, and the river looks like a {adjective} ribbon. I can even see our house! Your dad is in the backyard {verb ending in ing} with the dog.

Today my job is to lift steel beams for the new hospital. I move the beams {adverb} and set them down gently. The workers on the ground talk to me on a radio. When everything is going well, they say {exclamation}. When they need me to stop, they say {silly word}.

At lunch, a pigeon landed on my window and stared at my {food}. I named him Captain {noun}. When I get home tonight, let's {verb} together and eat {plural noun} for dessert. Love, Mom

title: The Grand Opening of the Bakery
text:
Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the grand opening of the Sweet Street Bakery! My name is Mayor Gomez, and I am so happy to be here.

Six months ago, this was an empty lot with weeds and a {adjective} old fence. Then the builders came. They brought a bulldozer, a cement mixer, and {number} {plural noun}. They worked {adverb} every single day, even when it was hot.

Now look at it! The bakery has a red roof, a big window, and an oven so large you could fit a {noun} inside. The baker, Mrs. Fig, says her first cake will be {food} flavored with sprinkles on top.

I would like to thank the builders, who {past tense verb} when I told them how proud I am. Now it is time to cut the ribbon. When I do, I want everyone to {verb} and cheer. Let the {verb ending in ing} begin!
